messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

ASSAY TYPE: Droplet-Based Bisulfite Sequencing ("Drop-BS") for High-Throughput Single-Cell DNA Methylome Library Preparation

REAGENTS USED:
  - Single-Nucleus Suspension (input nuclei for co-encapsulation)
  - Lysis Buffer (contains micrococcal nuclease, MNase, for single-nucleus lysis and genomic DNA fragmentation)
  - Droplet-Generation Oil (fluorinated carrier oil for water-in-oil droplet encapsulation, ~35 um diameter droplets)
  - Barcode Beads (hydrogel beads bearing unique, UV-photocleavable DNA barcode oligos)
  - End-Repair/Ligation Enzyme Mix (prepares fragmented scDNA ends for barcode ligation)
  - Ligation Mix (ligates released barcode oligos onto scDNA fragments)
  - Proteinase K (breaks droplets and digests protein to recover barcoded DNA for pooling)
  - Bisulfite Conversion Reagent (sodium bisulfite salt solution, converts unmethylated cytosines to uracil in droplets, ~99% conversion rate)
  - Random Primer (adds a second priming site to bisulfite-converted single-stranded DNA)
  - Klenow Fragment Mix (extends from the random primer to synthesize the second strand)
  - PCR Master Mix (used for both pre-amplification and indexing PCR)
  - P5/P7 Amplification Primers (pre-amplification adapter-addition primers)
  - i5/i7 Indexing Primers (sample-indexing primers for the final sequencing library)
  - EvaGreen Dye (intercalating dye for real-time monitoring of indexing PCR amplification)

STEPS:
1. scDNA encapsulation and fragmentation: Co-encapsulate single nuclei with lysis buffer (containing MNase) in oil droplets on a droplet-generation microfluidic device (~35 um droplets, ~10% single-occupancy, <0.5% double-occupancy) to lyse nuclei and fragment genomic DNA; incubate through a cold, room-temperature, and elevated-temperature step to complete lysis/fragmentation.
2. scDNA and barcode bead droplet pairing and fusion: Combine barcode beads with an end-repair/ligation enzyme mix, then fuse these bead-containing droplets with the reinjected scDNA droplets on a droplet-fusion microfluidic device (electrocoalescence), and add ligation mix to the fused droplets.
3. scDNA ligation and barcoding: Expose the fused droplets to UV light to release the barcoded oligos from the photocleavable linker on the beads, then carry out an extended (overnight) ligation step to tag each single cell's fragmented DNA with a unique barcode, followed by a brief high-temperature step to inactivate the ligation enzyme.
4. Recovery and bisulfite conversion: Break the droplets and digest with Proteinase K to pool the barcoded DNA; denature the pooled DNA to single strands, then co-encapsulate with bisulfite conversion reagent in droplets on a bisulfite-conversion microfluidic device, and incubate (high-temperature denaturation pulse followed by a longer moderate-temperature hold) to convert unmethylated cytosines to uracil (~99% conversion rate, validated with unmethylated lambda DNA).
5. Library preparation: Randomly prime the bisulfite-converted single-stranded DNA to add a second priming site, extend with a Klenow fragment polymerase to synthesize the complementary strand, then perform a low-cycle pre-amplification PCR to add P5/P7 adapter sequences, followed by an indexing PCR (with i5/i7 indexing primers) monitored in real time via EvaGreen intercalating-dye fluorescence to generate the final Illumina-compatible, barcoded single-cell bisulfite sequencing library.

INTERPRETATION: Successful library generation is confirmed by real-time EvaGreen fluorescence amplification during the indexing PCR step and by downstream sequencing metrics (per-cell read depth, bisulfite conversion rate ~99%, and species-mixing purity in control experiments), supporting use of Drop-BS to process up to 10,000 single cells within approximately 2 days for cell-type-resolved DNA methylome profiling of mixed cell lines and brain tissue.

module fluorescence

manifest nuclei_suspension
manifest lysis_buffer
manifest droplet_oil
manifest barcode_beads
manifest enzyme_mix
manifest ligation_mix
manifest proteinase_k
manifest bisulfite_reagent
manifest random_primer
manifest klenow_mix
manifest pcr_mastermix
manifest amp_primers
manifest index_primers
manifest evagreen_dye

instructions:

// Step 1: scDNA encapsulation and fragmentation - co-encapsulate single
// nuclei with lysis buffer (containing MNase) in oil droplets for
// single-nucleus lysis and genomic DNA fragmentation
nuclei = dispense 2 units of nuclei_suspension
lysis = dispense 2 units of lysis_buffer
oil1 = dispense 14 units of droplet_oil

scdna_droplet = mix nuclei with lysis for 5s
encapsulated = mix scdna_droplet with oil1 for 5s

heat encapsulated at 4c for 10m
heat encapsulated at 23c for 15m
heat encapsulated at 65c for 30m

// Step 2: scDNA and single barcode bead droplet pairing and fusion -
// barcode beads combined with end-repair/ligation enzyme mix, then fused
// with the reinjected scDNA droplets via dielectrophoresis
beads = dispense 5 units of barcode_beads
enzyme = dispense 40 units of enzyme_mix
bead_droplet = mix beads with enzyme for 5s

ligmix = dispense 150 units of ligation_mix
fused_droplet = mix encapsulated with bead_droplet for 5s
barcoded_droplet = mix fused_droplet with ligmix for 5s

// Step 3: scDNA ligation and barcoding - UV exposure releases barcoded
// oligos from the photocleavable linker on the beads, followed by
// overnight ligation and enzyme inactivation
heat barcoded_droplet at 25c for 8m
heat barcoded_droplet at 16c for 1080m
heat barcoded_droplet at 70c for 15m

// Break droplets and digest with Proteinase K to recover barcoded DNA
// (SPRI bead purification not modeled)
pk = dispense 15 units of proteinase_k
digested = mix barcoded_droplet with pk for 30s
heat digested at 65c for 120m

// Step 4: Droplet-based bisulfite conversion - denature to single-stranded
// DNA, combine with bisulfite conversion reagent, and convert in droplets
heat digested at 95c for 90s
heat digested at 4c for 2m

bisulfite = dispense 130 units of bisulfite_reagent
bisulfite_droplet = mix digested with bisulfite for 10s

heat bisulfite_droplet at 95c for 5m
heat bisulfite_droplet at 54c for 60m

// Step 5: Library preparation - random priming to add a second priming
// site to the bisulfite-converted DNA
primer = dispense 1 units of random_primer
primed = mix bisulfite_droplet with primer for 5s

heat primed at 95c for 3m
heat primed at 4c for 2m

klenow = dispense 8 units of klenow_mix
extension_mix = mix primed with klenow for 10s

heat extension_mix at 4c for 5m
heat extension_mix at 25c for 5m
heat extension_mix at 37c for 60m

// Pre-amplification PCR (5 cycles) to add P5/P7 adapter sequences
mastermix1 = dispense 25 units of pcr_mastermix
ampprimers = dispense 3 units of amp_primers
preamp_mix = mix extension_mix with mastermix1 for 10s
preamp_reaction = mix preamp_mix with ampprimers for 10s

heat preamp_reaction at 98c for 30s

repeat 5 times {
    heat preamp_reaction at 98c for 10s
    heat preamp_reaction at 58c for 30s
    heat preamp_reaction at 72c for 30s
}

heat preamp_reaction at 72c for 60s

// Indexing PCR amplification (3 cycles) with i5/i7 indexing primers,
// monitored in real time via EvaGreen fluorescence
mastermix2 = dispense 25 units of pcr_mastermix
idxprimers = dispense 3 units of index_primers
dye = dispense 3 units of evagreen_dye

index_mix = mix preamp_reaction with mastermix2 for 10s
index_reaction = mix index_mix with idxprimers for 10s
labeled_reaction = mix index_reaction with dye for 10s

heat labeled_reaction at 98c for 30s

repeat 3 times {
    heat labeled_reaction at 98c for 10s
    heat labeled_reaction at 62c for 30s
    heat labeled_reaction at 72c for 30s
}

heat labeled_reaction at 72c for 60s

// Detect successful indexed-library amplification via EvaGreen
// fluorescence signal
library_signal = detect fluorescence on labeled_reaction for 30s

if (library_signal < 50) {
    dispose labeled_reaction
}

metadata.protocol_name: Droplet-based bisulfite sequencing for high-throughput profiling of single-cell DNA methylomes, Drop-BS (Zhang, Ma, Liu, Zhu, Zhou, Li, Meana, Gonzalez-Maeso & Lu, Nature Communications 2023)

sources.title: Droplet-based bisulfite sequencing for high-throughput profiling of single-cell DNA methylomes
Droplet-based bisulfite sequencing for high-throughput profiling of single-cell DNA methylomes (preprint)

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code translates the paper's five-major-step Drop-BS workflow (scDNA encapsulation/fragmentation, barcode bead droplet pairing/fusion, scDNA ligation/barcoding, droplet-based bisulfite conversion, and library preparation via random priming + indexing PCR) run across three microfluidic devices (droplet-generation, droplet-fusion, and bisulfite-conversion devices), as described in the paper's overview of the five-step process and Figs. 1-2. Because BioScript has no primitives for microfluidic droplet generation rate/occupancy control, dielectrophoretic droplet fusion/electrocoalescence, UV photocleavage of bead-bound barcodes, or SPRI-bead-based DNA cleanup, these operations are approximated using the closest available primitives: droplet pairing/fusion and barcode release are modeled as sequential 'mix' operations; UV-triggered barcode release is folded into the room-temperature incubation step immediately preceding the extended ligation hold rather than modeled as a distinct light-exposure primitive; and SPRI purification steps between the ligation, bisulfite-conversion, and library-prep stages are intentionally omitted (noted inline in the .bs file) since BioScript exposes no bead-based nucleic-acid cleanup primitive. Specific incubation temperatures/durations for lysis/fragmentation, ligation, Klenow extension, and PCR cycling (e.g. 4c/23c/65c encapsulation hold, 16c overnight ligation, 98/58/72c and 98/62/72c thermocycling) are typical values for these enzymatic steps (MNase fragmentation, T4 ligase, Klenow fragment, standard two-step PCR) rather than paper-confirmed exact figures, since the available preprint/published-article excerpts describe the five-step workflow and device-level timing (droplet generation, fusion, and bisulfite-device run times) but not every individual reagent-incubation temperature/duration; these are flagged as illustrative assumptions consistent with standard molecular-biology practice for each named enzyme/reagent. The paper's droplet generation/fusion throughput rates (~3000 scDNA droplets/s, ~132 barcode-fusion droplets/s), device-level processing-time benchmarks (10 min droplet generation, 36 min fusion, 30 min bisulfite conversion for ~2000 cells), the species-mixing purity validation experiment, and the downstream sequencing/bioinformatic methylome analysis (mixed cell lines, mouse and human brain tissue) are hardware-throughput, validation, or off-chip sequencing/analysis sub-experiments with no corresponding BioScript primitive, and are intentionally not modeled; only the core five-step on-droplet library-construction protocol is captured here.

numeric_mismatches.field: heat encapsulated at 4c for 10m / 23c for 15m / 65c for 30m (Step 1 lysis/fragmentation)
numeric_mismatches.note: The paper confirms MNase-based lysis/fragmentation occurs in ~35 um droplets with ~10% single-occupancy, but the specific incubation temperature/time sequence in the .bs file is a typical MNase digestion protocol assumption, not an exact value extracted from the available paper excerpts.

The paper's overview confirms an extended ligation step tags each cell's DNA with a barcode, but the specific 16c/18h duration is a standard overnight-ligation assumption rather than a paper-confirmed figure.

BioScript has no light-exposure/UV primitive; the barcode-release step is folded into the preceding room-temperature incubation ('heat barcoded_droplet at 25c for 8m') rather than modeled as a distinct optical operation.

numeric_mismatches.note: The paper's workflow includes SPRI-based DNA cleanup between major steps; BioScript has no bead-based nucleic-acid purification primitive, so these cleanup steps are omitted, as flagged directly in the .bs file's comments.
